newsitem.title: FINLAND: New Finnish jobless statistics to cut unemployment.
newsitem.headline: New Finnish jobless statistics to cut unemployment.

text.p: A change in the way Finnish unemployment is measured is likely to lower the jobless rate figure, but only by less than one percentage point, a Statistics Finland (SF) official said on Thursday.
As of the beginning of this year, people who are laid off for fixed periods will no longer be classified as unemployed, SF said in a statement.

"It would have a less than one percentage point impact on the unemployment rate in the long run," said senior statistician Salme Kiiski, adding that the impact would vary from month to month. She declined to give precise figures.
The new method of counting the unemployed will first show up in March, when SF is scheduled to publish jobless figures for January, SF said.
Kiiski said the change would not radically alter the Finnish unemploymnent picture.

"You cannot say that statistics are being used to cut unemployment in half," said Kiski, referring to the government's stated goal of halving unemployment to 8-9 percent by the end of its term of office in 1999.
In November, the jobless rate was 15.9 percent.
